title: Optimized protocol for brain and head kidney catalase activity in zebrafish
author: Caio Maximino
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.rumd6u6
materials: Dilute 0.34 ml 30% hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) with phosphate buffer to 100 ml, reaching a final concentration of 30 mM H 2 O 2 .

Make seven serial dilutions of 30 mM H 2 O 2 (down to 0.234375 mM) in phosphate buffer Phosphate buffer (0.1 M, pH 7.3) [80 ml 0.1 M Na2HPO4 (13.8 g Na2HPO4⋅H2O/liter dH2O) 20 ml 0.1 M NaH2PO4 (26.8 g NaH2PO4⋅7H2O/liter dH2O)] Contributed by users Hydrogen peroxide 30% Merck Millipore (EMD Millipore) Catalog #822287.1000 12x75 mm high clarity polypropylene test tubes Corning Catalog #352063

H 2 O 2 quantification 1. Allow reagents to equilibrate, and pour in a Quartz cuvette. 2. Read on a spectrophotometer at 240 nm. ATTENTION All analyses should be made with at least three technical replicates Thoroughly rinse the cuvettes with distilled water to remove contaminants before each replicate
Re-suspend the homogenate by vortexing, if needed
Carefully transfer the homogenate to the cuvette.

Prepare reagents for the linearity curve: 1. Prepare phosphate buffer (0.1 M, pH 7.3) 2. steps.title: Sacrifice and Dissect Animal
steps.instruction: Sacrifice the animal using ice-cold water (< 12 ºC) followed by spinal transection. Carefully dissect the brain and head kidney.

steps.title: Homogenize Tissue
steps.instruction: Homogenize the dissected tissue in 2 ml of Phosphate buffer (PB) (0.1 M, pH 7.3).

substeps.instruction: Prepare PB (0.1 M, pH 7.3) by mixing 80 ml 0.1 M Na2HPO4 (13.8 g Na2HPO4⋅H2O/liter dH2O) and 20 ml 0.1 M NaH2PO4 (26.8 g NaH2PO4⋅7H2O/liter dH2O).
Note: Tissues can be kept frozen (- 20 ºC) for up to 6 months.

steps.title: Perform Catalase Activity Assay
steps.instruction: Add 1 ml H2O2 (30 mM) solution and immediately record the response.

steps.title: Determine Linearity and Curve Parameters
steps.instruction: Enter data in two columns ('x' for concentration and 'y' for response) and perform linear regression using the chemCal package in R (version 0.2.1, Xubuntu 16.04).

substeps.instruction: Install and load chemCal: if(!require(chemCal)){ install.packages('chemCal') library(chemCal)}
Fit linear model: m <- lm(y ~ x, data = your_data)
Analyze results using summary(m) and calplot(m).

Verify linearity: Correlation coefficients > 0.98 suggest linearity. Check error residuals for uniform distribution, average zero, constant variance, and absence of atypical samples. Optionally, use an F-test to compare linear vs. quadratic model fits.

steps.title: Calculate Sensitivity (LOD and LOQ)
steps.instruction: Determine the limit of detection (LOD) and limit of quantification (LOQ) using the linear model parameters in chemCal.

substeps.instruction: Calculate LOD using lod(m, alpha = 0.01, beta = 0.5).
Calculate LOQ using loq(m, n = your_n), substituting 'your_n' with the number of technical replicates.

steps.title: Assess Precision
steps.instruction: Determine the precision of the assay by calculating the relative standard deviation (RSD = 100 * s / |x̄|), where s is the sample standard deviation and x̄ is the sample mean.

substeps.instruction: Assess intra-run precision (repeatability): Run three technical replicates for the lowest, intermediate, and highest H2O2 concentrations and calculate the RSD for each. RSDs > 15% indicate low precision.

Assess intermediate precision (inter-run precision): Run three technical replicates for the lowest, intermediate, and highest H2O2 concentrations on two different days and assess the RSD. RSDs > 15% indicate low intermediate precision.

steps.title: Determine Accuracy
steps.instruction: Establish accuracy after linearity, sensitivity, and precision are determined by running another calibration curve with at least three technical replicates for the entire range of concentrations.

substeps.instruction: Generate predicted values (xi) using a weighted linear model in chemCal. Weights are derived from the accuracy determination curve: weights <- with(new_data, { yx <- split(y, x); ybar <- sapply(yx, mean); s <- round(sapply(yx, sd), digits = 2); w <- round(1 / (s^2), digits = 3) }).
Calculate the weighted model: n <- lm(y ~ x, w = weights, data = new_data.means).
Use inverse.predict to find predicted values for concentrations: 30, 15, 7.5, 3.75, 1.875, 0.9375, 0.46875, and 0.234375 μM.
Calculate accuracy at each level using the formula: Accuracy = ([xi - xv] / xv) * 100, where xv is the measured absorbance.
